title: Maximal-adic graded algebra and cumulative length-polynomial bridge
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Form $S=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}(R)=\bigoplus_{i\ge0}\mathfrak m^i/\mathfrak m^{i+1}$ with its degree-zero $k$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Then $S$ is a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]; for any finite generating list $y_1,\ldots,y_t$ of $\mathfrak m$, its degree-one classes generate $S$, and their degree-$i$ monomials span $S_i$ over $k$. Every $S_i$ is finite-dimensional, its composition length over $R$ equals $\dim_k S_i$, and, for every integer $n\ge1$, $R/\mathfrak m^n$ has finite composition length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], with
$$H_R(n):=\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\dim_k S_i\ge1.$$
Moreover, if $P\in\mathbf Q[X]$ satisfies $\dim_k S_i=P(i)$ for all sufficiently large integers $i$, there exist $Q\in\mathbf Q[X]$, $Q\ne0$, with strictly positive leading coefficient and $N\ge1$ such that $H_R(n)=Q(n)$ for every integer $n\ge N$. The polynomial $P$ is allowed to be zero.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose generators $y_1,\ldots,y_t$ of $\mathfrak m$, allowing $t=0$. The ring and scalar laws of [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring-structure] give $S_0=k$ and $S_aS_b\subseteq S_{a+b}$. For any such list, induction on $i$ shows that $\mathfrak m^i$ is generated as an $R$-ideal by the degree-$i$ monomials in the $y_j$: degree zero uses the empty monomial $1$; multiply the asserted generating expressions by $\mathfrak m=(y_1,\ldots,y_t)$ for the successor step. Reducing their coefficients modulo $\mathfrak m$ shows that their classes span $S_i$ over $k$, since $\mathfrak m\mathfrak m^i\subseteq\mathfrak m^{i+1}$. There are finitely many such monomials. Consequently every $S_i$ is finite-dimensional, and every homogeneous element is a polynomial in the degree-one classes. A direct-sum element has finitely many homogeneous components, so those classes generate $S$. This verifies precisely [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].

proof.text: Put $d_i=\dim_kS_i$. An $R$-submodule of $S_i$ is exactly a $k$-subspace: for a scalar $\bar a\in k$ choose any lift $a\in R$, and use that $\mathfrak m S_i=0$. Thus a basis flag has $d_i$ strict inclusions, and every strict submodule chain has at most $d_i$ inclusions because dimension strictly increases at each inclusion. The chain definition [def-weil-pbc-module-length] therefore gives $\mathrm{length}_R(S_i)=d_i<\infty$. This includes $i=0$, where $S_0=k\ne0$ and $d_0=1$.

For every $i\ge0$ the maps sending $x\bmod\mathfrak m^{i+1}$ to its class in $R/\mathfrak m^{i+1}$ and reducing a class modulo $\mathfrak m^i$ give an exact sequence $0\to S_i\to R/\mathfrak m^{i+1}\to R/\mathfrak m^i\to0$: the first map is injective, the second is surjective, and its kernel is exactly the image of $\mathfrak m^i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact]. Starting with $R/\mathfrak m^0=0$, induction gives finite length and $H_R(n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}d_i$. Since $d_0=1$ and all $d_i\ge0$, this sum is at least one for $n\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive; the power-filtration identity immediately before Tag 00K8

proof.text: Choose an integer $a\ge1$ such that $d_i=P(i)$ for all $i\ge a$. Write $P(X)=\sum_{p=0}^{D}c_pX^p$, taking $D=0,c_0=0$ if $P=0$. For each $p$, let $F_p(X)=\sum_{j=0}^{p}b_j\binom{p+1}{j}X^{p+1-j}/(p+1)$, using the rational numbers of [lem-trf-rational-power-sum-formula]. Its formula says $F_p(n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}i^p$. Set $A(X)=\sum_{p=0}^{D}c_pF_p(X)$ and $Q(X)=A(X)+H_R(a)-A(a)$. Interchanging these finite sums gives $A(n)-A(a)=\sum_{i=a}^{n-1}P(i)$ for $n\ge a$. The preceding length identity therefore gives $Q(n)=H_R(n)$. This is the discrete summation of Tag 00JZ written with explicit power-sum polynomials, including $P=0$.

source.place: Tag 00JZ, lemma-numerical-polynomial; explicit power-sum formula sum_range_pow, Mathlib/NumberTheory/Bernoulli.lean:295–298

proof.text: Because $Q(n)=H_R(n)\ge1$ for $n\ge a$, $Q$ is nonzero. Let $d=\deg Q$ and $c$ its nonzero leading coefficient. If $d=0$, then $c=Q(a)\ge1$. If $d\ge1$ and $c<0$, write $Q(X)=cX^d+\sum_{j<d}q_jX^j$ and put $C=\sum_{j<d}|q_j|$. For any integer $n\ge1$, the absolute value of the lower-degree sum is at most $Cn^{d-1}$. Choose an integer $n\ge a$ with $n>C/(-c)$. Then $Q(n)\le n^{d-1}(cn+C)<0$, a contradiction. Hence $c>0$, and $N=a$ has all the required properties.

lean.statement: theorem maximalAdicGradedLengthBridge (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : ∃ 𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule (ResidueField R) (Ideal.associatedGraded (maximalIdeal R)), (∀ i : ℕ, (𝒜 i : Set (Ideal.associatedGraded (maximalIdeal R))) = Set.range (DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece (maximalIdeal R)) i)) ∧ ∃ (_grading : GradedAlgebra 𝒜), GradedAlgebra.IsStandard (k := ResidueField R) 𝒜 ∧ (∀ (t : ℕ) (y : Fin t → ↥(maximalIdeal R ^ 1)), Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin t ↦ (y j).val)) = maximalIdeal R → Algebra.adjoin (ResidueField R) (Set.range (fun j : Fin t ↦ DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece (maximalIdeal R)) 1 (Submodule.Quotient.mk (y j)))) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, Submodule.span (ResidueField R) (Set.range (fun f : Fin i → Fin t ↦ ∏ j : Fin i, DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece (maximalIdeal R)) 1 (Submodule.Quotient.mk (y (f j))))) = 𝒜 i) ∧ (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite (ResidueField R) (𝒜 i) ∧ Module.length R (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece (maximalIdeal R) i) = (Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (𝒜 i) : ℕ∞)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → IsFiniteLength R (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n) ∧ Module.length R (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n) = ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (𝒜 i)) : ℕ∞) ∧ 1 ≤ Module.length R (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n)) ∧ (∀ P : Polynomial ℚ, (∃ a : ℕ, ∀ i : ℕ, a ≤ i → (Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (𝒜 i) : ℚ) = P.eval (i : ℚ)) → ∃ Q : Polynomial ℚ, Q ≠ 0 ∧ 0 < Q.leadingCoeff ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → ((Module.length R (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n)).toNat : ℚ) = Q.eval (n : ℚ))
